## Pi worker

You run as a pstack worker: an independent Pi process in tmux that a parent session started with the `pstack_worker` tool. Your brief is your whole task. Read every skill the brief names before other work. You have no `pstack_worker` tool by default. Without it, when the brief or a skill asks for another worker, do that work yourself, or name the request in your report and stop. When your assignment sets `capabilities.spawn: true`, as for a sub-coordinator, you have `pstack_worker` and own your children's runs. They live under your workspace's `.pi/pstack/runs/`, their wakes come to you, and you collect and judge their results yourself. Nesting stops at three levels (root, sub-coordinator, worker), so your children cannot get `capabilities.spawn: true`. Write your final report to `report.md` in the worker directory the brief names. Save each check you ran as a receipt under that directory's `evidence/`, and register it with `pstack_evidence` `record`. A readonly worker cannot write files. Its final reply is its report, and it names each check it ran there, with the command and its result, in place of receipts. Never claim a check you did not run. The parent reads your report, your receipts, and your session file after you settle.

spans.replacement:
**Workers.** A subagent here is a pstack worker: an independent Pi process in tmux. To spawn one, write `brief.md` and `assignment.json` under `.pi/pstack/runs/<runId>/workers/<workerId>/` and call `pstack_worker` with `{ action: "spawn", runId, assignmentPath }`. The assignment's `role` picks the role instruction: `poteto`, `explorer`, `investigator`, `candidate`, `judge`, `verifier`, `reviewer`, `owner`, `watcher`, `comment-sicko`, or `general`. Its `workspace` is `{ mode: "worktree", inputCommit }` for a writable worker or `{ mode: "readonly", path }` for a worker limited to `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `bash_readonly`, and MCP tools. `bash_readonly` is an OS-sandboxed read-only shell that allows `git`, `gh`, and network reads and blocks writes. Its `model` is a model spec or `inherit-parent`. Its `capabilities` default to `{ mcp: "inherit", env: "inherit", externalWrite: false }`, with `spawn` false. A default written as a family and level, such as `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` or `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast`, means that family's model at that thinking level, fast variant included. Spawn returns at once with a tmux attach command. A `pstack-worker` wake message reports each worker that settles. Then call `collect` for its report. Use `inspect` for live state, `steer` to redirect a live worker, and `abort` to stop one. A worker has no `pstack_worker` tool by default, so it does delegated work itself. A worker you assign `capabilities.spawn: true` has `pstack_worker` within the depth limit of three levels (you, it, and its workers). It owns its children's runs and receives their wakes, and its own children cannot get `capabilities.spawn: true`. A container worker has `workspace: { mode: "container", inputCommit }` and runs a writable clone inside the container that `.pi/environment.json` configures. Spawn refuses it with `ContainerUnavailable` until a container environment is installed. Then a step that names a local fallback uses it, and a step without one reports itself blocked. A watch loop is a `pstack_worker` spawn with `kind: "watch"`. Its `watch.argv` runs in tmux, and its exit wakes you. A fixed interval uses `["sleep", "<seconds>"]`, and an event uses the watcher's command. A watch fires once. Spawn it again after each wake until the stop predicate holds. After a parent restart, re-arm each open watch loop from the run's `TODO.md` or plan, because nothing spawns it again on its own. The model rule is `~/.pi/agent/pstack/models.json`, and each of its role keys is a line.

**Defaults for every `pstack_worker` spawn.** Keep working after the spawn returns (a `steer` of a live worker too), because waiting on one worker holds your turn while other reports wait. spans.original: **Fork when new work needs a worker's built state,** such as its checkout, uncommitted changes, or a running process. Message a worker only for a follow-up on the same work. Never message one to check on it, because a message restarts an idle agent.
spans.replacement: **Fork when new work needs a worker's built state,** such as its checkout, uncommitted changes, or a running process. To fork, once that worker settles, spawn a fresh worker whose `workspace.inputCommit` is the source worker's worktree `HEAD`, with the source's report in its brief. Have the source commit its changes in its own worktree before it settles, and have the new brief restart any process the work needs, because neither carries over otherwise. Steer a worker only for a follow-up on the same work. Never steer one to check on it, because a steer starts a turn on an idle worker. Use `inspect` instead.

spans.original: `unlimited`, `large`, `medium`, and `small` set the effort token of every real slug, panel entries included, to `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, or `medium`. The effort token is the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`, on the ladder `max` > `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. If the result is not a detected slug, use the same family's detected slug with the highest effort at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. So `unlimited` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` into `claude-opus-5-5-max`. Grok slugs top out at `xhigh`, so under `unlimited` the fallback puts Grok at `xhigh` and keeps `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` as it is. `large` keeps both defaults. `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium` and `grok-4.7-medium-fast`.
spans.replacement: `unlimited`, `large`, `medium`, and `small` set the thinking level of every real model spec, panel entries included, to `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, or `medium`. The level is the `:<level>` suffix, on the ladder `max` > `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. If the model does not list that level, use its highest listed level at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. So `unlimited` turns `<provider>/claude-opus-5-5:xhigh` into `<provider>/claude-opus-5-5:max`. A model whose levels top out at `xhigh` stays at `xhigh` under `unlimited`. `large` keeps both defaults. `small` sets both to `:medium`.
